question: Which of the following molecules has triangular plane geometry?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "BF3" -> "trigonal planar electron geometry" -> "triangular plane geometry" -> 95%
CHAIN: "NH3" -> "trigonal pyramidal electron geometry" -> "not triangular plane geometry" -> 90%
CHAIN: "AsH3" -> "trigonal pyramidal electron geometry" -> "not triangular plane geometry" -> 90%
CHAIN: "XeO3" -> "trigonal pyramidal electron geometry" -> "not triangular plane geometry" -> 85%
CHAIN: "ClF3" -> "T-shaped electron geometry" -> "not triangular plane geometry" -> 90%
analysis: The molecule BF3 (boron trifluoride) has a triangular planar geometry. This is because boron, the central atom, forms three bonds with fluorine atoms and has no lone pairs, resulting in a planar structure with 120-degree bond angles. In contrast, NH3 (ammonia) and AsH3 (arsine) have trigonal pyramidal geometries due to the presence of a lone pair on the nitrogen and arsenic atoms, respectively. XeO3 (xenon trioxide) has a pyramidal shape due to the presence of lone pairs on the xenon atom. ClF3 (chlorine trifluoride) has a T-shaped geometry due to the presence of two lone pairs on the chlorine atom.
